cases.CREATE: Fresh private empty canonical root; successful cleanup removes only it; repeated cleanup succeeds and path refuses.
cases.PARALLEL: Two simultaneous owners have distinct inodes and paths; retiring one preserves the other.
cases.INPUT: Missing, relative, noncanonical, NUL and overlong bases fail without new nodes.
cases.SYMLINK: Selected symlink is rejected without mutation of its target.
cases.PERMISSIONS: Nonprivate base and writable ancestor refuse without repairing modes; restrictive umask never changes global state.
cases.FILESYSTEM: The Windows-mounted filesystem is refused and has no new nodes.
cases.BUSY: Independent flock blocks cleanup without deleting or invalidating; release permits cleanup.
cases.CONTENTS: Unexpected regular file, symlink and directory each survive failed cleanup; owner stays invalidated after contents are removed externally.
cases.REPLACEMENT: Leaf replacement, ancestor replacement and changed mode refuse and preserve both old and replacement nodes; restored paths do not restore authority.
cases.OWNER: Wrong-thread path and cleanup refuse while the legitimate owner remains usable.
cases.ORPHAN: Destructor and abrupt process death preserve their exact roots; new ownership never adopts them.
cases.SUPERVISOR: Cooperative exact child exit is independently observed; supervisor lock blocks retirement through closed state until destructor releases it.
cases.FORCED: Uncooperative shutdown requires exact SIGKILL and wait; retirement follows independently observed child death and supervisor destruction.
cases.ORACLE: An intentionally wrong expectation that a populated directory is empty must be detected.
